protocol.name: AAuth PS Authorization Access (Three-Party)
protocol.description: The AAuth flow closest to OAuth authorization code: an agent with its own key obtains a person token, is challenged by the resource with a resource token, obtains an auth token from the person server, and signs every request. Aligned with draft-hardt-oauth-aauth-protocol-11.

entities.name: Person
entities.description: The person the agent acts for. Approves at their own person server, on their own timeline

entities.name: Agent
entities.description: Holds a signing key. Signs every request with it. Identified as aauth:local@domain

entities.name: Agent Provider
entities.description: Issues the agent token that binds the agent's key to its identifier

entities.name: Person Server
entities.description: Chosen by the person, not the resource. Issues person tokens and auth tokens, runs consent

entities.name: Resource
entities.description: Verifies signatures and tokens. Signs a resource token describing what it requires

phases.name: Agent Token (identity)
phases.description: The agent proves key possession to its agent provider and receives an agent token. No resource is involved

phases.name: Person Token (who the agent acts for)
phases.description: The agent asks its person server for a token naming this resource

phases.name: Resource Token (what the resource requires)
phases.description: The resource signs a description of the access it needs before it will serve

phases.name: Auth Token (consent)
phases.description: The person server runs consent and issues the auth token bound to the agent's key

phases.name: Signed Resource Access
phases.description: Every request carries an HTTP Message Signature and the token in Signature-Key

flows.label: Prove key possession (platform specific, see AAuth Bootstrap)
agent token (aa-agent+jwt) with cnf = agent key and ps = person server URL

annotations.text: Portable identity. Verifiable by any resource from the agent provider's JWKS, with no registration at the resource.

flows.label: POST person_token_endpoint with resource = URL, HTTP Sig with agent token
First use of this resource? Show its metadata and ask (202 interaction, or a tap out of band)
person token (aa-person+jwt) with aud = resource, directed sub, cnf = agent key

annotations.text: Identity only, no scope. The sub is directed per resource, so resources cannot correlate the person.

flows.label: POST authorization_endpoint, or any call, HTTP Sig with person token
401 or 200 with resource token (aa-resource+jwt) with aud = PS, ps, sub, presented_jti, scope

annotations.text: The resource, not the client, authors and signs the authorization request. OAuth has no equivalent.

flows.label: POST auth_token_endpoint with resource_token and presented_token, HTTP Sig with agent token
Consent card = resource metadata, resource-asserted scope, agent-asserted justification (202 interaction)

annotations.text: Pending is a state, not an error. The agent polls the pending URL while the person decides.

flows.label: Approve, deny, or ask the agent a clarification
auth token (aa-auth+jwt) with aud = resource, ps, sub, scope, cnf = agent key
GET /api with Signature-Key sig=jwt and HTTP Message Signature

annotations.text: Never bearer. A stolen token is useless without the agent's private key.
